title: Keep price alerts working while users add and remove them

blocks.text: The trading screen lets each user set price alerts: "tell me when NOVA goes above 182.50". The market feed publishes every tick on its own thread, a few thousand a second, to the alerts held in `AlertRegistry`; users add and remove alerts from the UI threads whenever they like, a few times an hour each. A screen has a few dozen alerts at most.

The first version failed in production twice: once a tick was lost for half the alerts with an exception in the feed thread, just as someone added an alert, and once adding an alert froze a user's screen for four seconds while one alert was slow to send its e-mail.

Finish `src/main/java/practice/AlertRegistry.java`: decide how the alerts are held, and write `subscribe`, `unsubscribe` and `publish`. When you're done, a tick reaches every alert that was subscribed when the publish began, a publish never fails because of what the UI threads do, and adding or removing an alert never waits for a publish. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a published tick reaches every subscribed alert once, and an unsubscribed alert not at all
a publish still reaches the remaining alerts when another thread subscribes while it runs
a subscribe from another thread returns while an alert is still handling a tick

origin.section: Once Another Thread Writes, a Fail-Fast Walk Fails at Random; a Small Listener List Needs a Snapshot

concepts: A small list that threads share, read far more often than it is written, fits CopyOnWriteArrayList: a walk never fails and takes no lock, so a write never waits for it.
